subject: Chemistry
title: Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment.

hook.text: Rutherford fired alpha particles at gold foil. Most passed through—but some bounced straight back. He was stunned.

buildup.text: If Thomson's plum pudding model was right, all particles should pass through the diffuse positive charge.

discovery.text: One in 8,000 particles bounced back. Rutherford concluded all positive charge was concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.

twist.text: He compared it to firing artillery at tissue paper and having shells bounce back. The atom was mostly empty space.

climax.text: The nucleus contains 99.97% of the atom's mass but only 1/100,000th of its volume. Atoms are almost entirely nothing.

punchline.text: Most passed through, a few bounced back. A tiny dense core in a cloud of nothing.

quiz.question: What did Rutherford conclude from alpha particles bouncing back?
options: The atom's positive charge is concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus
Atoms are solid spheres with no internal structure
Electrons orbit in fixed rings around the nucleus

details.summary: In 1911 Ernest Rutherford's team fired alpha particles at thin gold foil and found that most passed through while a tiny fraction bounced straight back. This proved that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space.
details.whyItMatters: Rutherford's nuclear model replaced Thomson's plum pudding and remains the foundation of our understanding of atomic structure. It revealed that matter is overwhelmingly empty space.
takeaways: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil undeflected
A few particles bounced back, implying a dense central nucleus
The atom is mostly empty space with mass concentrated in the nucleus

faq.question: What did Rutherford mean when he said it was like firing shells at tissue paper?
faq.answer: Alpha particles are relatively massive and fast. If Thomson's uniform pudding model were correct, none should bounce back from thin foil. The fact that some deflected dramatically was as shocking as cannonballs bouncing off paper, implying a concentrated target inside the atom.

faq.question: What problem did Rutherford's model leave unsolved?
faq.answer: Classical physics predicted that orbiting electrons should continuously emit radiation and spiral into the nucleus within nanoseconds. Rutherford's model could not explain why atoms are stable, a problem that required Bohr's quantized orbit model and ultimately quantum mechanics to resolve.
